block.title: Hi_atexit is safe from an explicitly initialized main entry

claim.p: The linked hi_atexit program is safe once main starts with the initialized state described here. All its library calls are proved, including error paths. The proof checks that the required memory actually exists and that no field is owned twice.

block.p: Before main starts, the model allocates a thread object and initializes its pointers and stream links. It also sets the single-thread flag. This preparation can fail on allocation, but succeeds for the linked loader image. It leaves other bytes and pointer capabilities unchanged.

Real programs run startup code before they call main. This proof does not verify that code; it prepares memory explicitly instead. The loaded program has no thread object and a zero single-thread flag, so it cannot supply this entry state by itself. Keeping constructors in the linked program does not perform these preparations. Verifying real startup remains a later campaign task. The safety result allows output to fail.
